title: Tracking Facebook interactions in Google Tag Manager

body_html:
To track Facebook interactions like (pun intended!) Like, Un-Like and Comments in Universal Analytics (UA) via Google Tag Manager (GTM), you need to follow a series of steps — and there are multiple pitfalls along the way. Here’s my findings, as a step-by-step guide.

Setup a Facebook App

If you have a Facebook-account, you’re also (almost) a Facebook Developer!
Go to developer.facebook.com
Click on “My Apps”, then on “Register as a developer” and finally on “Register Now”.
Have your phone ready (to recieve a confirmation-code) and follow the steps to register.

When registration is complete, click on “My Apps” and “Add a new app”.
Choose “www”
Give your app a name (could be the name of your website), and click on “Create New Facebook App ID”.
Now choose a category and create the app.

In the “Setup the Facebook SDK for JavaScript”-block, copy your app’s id (a long string of numbers), looking similar to this:

FB.init({
      appId      : '615880505229182'
    });

— and save it for later, we’re gonna use it in GTM in a few minutes.
Fill out your site’s url and proceed.

Now skip the rest of the intro, go to your app’s Settings. In the url-field, you’ll see the url, you wrote in the previous step.
If you’re working directly with that url, everything is fine.

If you’re working on a localhost or other test-environment, you need to add the url’s of this/those to Facebook’s oAuth-setting, as Facebook requires a 2-way communication.

Click on “Advanced” and find the section “Valid OAuth redirect URIs”.
Here, add the url’s of your test-environment/s.

If your test-environment is not reachable from “the outside” (like localhost), you might want to use a tool like localtunnel.me. localtunnel itself requires node.js — if you don’t have that, go to nodejs.org and download/install node.js for your platform.

After the installation is complete, go to the node.js prompt and type:

npm install -g localtunnel

— to install localtunnel. When that is done, start a tunnel:

lt --port 8000

You will receive a “tunnel” to your localhost. Copy this, and add it to the oAuth-list mentioned before.

Now, let’s go to GTM (assuming you already have an account there).

Google Tag Manager

Go to “Variables”, click on “New”, then on “Constant”.
Name your variable CN Facebook App ID and, as value, paste your Facebook App Id — in the example I created before, it was 615880505229182.

We need 3 more variables, of the type “Data Layer Variable”:

Name : DL socialAction
Data Layer Variable Name : socialAction

Name : DL socialNetwork
Data Layer Variable Name : socialNetwork

Name : DL socialTarget
Data Layer Variable Name : socialTarget

All done? Now go to “Triggers”, click on “New”, then “Custom Event”.
Under “Fire on”, paste the value socialInt, name your trigger EV socialInt and save it.

Finally, move to Tags, click on “New” and then on “Custom HTML”.
Name your tag CU Facebook Init and paste the following code under “Configure tag”:


<div id="fb-root"></div>

<script>
  window.fbAsyncInit = function() {
    FB.init({
      appId      : "{{CN Facebook App ID}}",
      xfbml      : true,
      version    : "v2.5"
    });
    
    if (typeof FB !== "undefined"){
      FB.Event.subscribe("edge.create",
        function(targetURL) {
          dataLayer.push({
          "event": "socialInt",
          "socialNetwork": "Facebook",
          "socialAction": "Like",
          "socialTarget": targetURL
          });
        }
      );

      FB.Event.subscribe("edge.remove", function(location){
        dataLayer.push({
          "event": "socialInt",
          "socialNetwork": "Facebook",
          "socialAction": "Unlike",
          "socialTarget": location
        });
      });
      
      FB.Event.subscribe("comment.create", function(){
        dataLayer.push({
          "event": "socialInt",
          "socialNetwork": "Facebook",
          "socialAction": "Comment Create",
          "socialTarget": window.location.href
        });
      });
      
      FB.Event.subscribe("comment.remove", function(){
        dataLayer.push({
          "event": "socialInt",
          "socialNetwork": "Facebook",
          "socialAction": "Comment Remove",
          "socialTarget": window.location.href
        });
      });
                  
    }
  };
(function(d,s,id){var js,fjs=d.getElementsByTagName(s)[0];if (d.getElementById(id)){return;}js=d.createElement(s);js.id=id;js.src="//connect.facebook.net/{{LT Facebook Language}}/sdk.js";fjs.parentNode.insertBefore(js,fjs);}(document,"script","facebook-jssdk"));
</script>

Add the trigger “All pages” and save the tag.
Almost there!

Now, create a new tag, select “Google Analytics” and then “Universal Analytics”.
Fill out your tracking ID (your UA code).
Under “Track Type”, choose “Social”.
Fill out “Network” with {{DL socialNetwork}}, “Action” with {{DL socialAction}} and “Action Target” with {{DL socialTarget}}.

Name your tag UA Social Media, fire on EV socialInt (the trigger you created before) and save it.

Preview your container, and then go to a page with the container snippet installed.
Verify that the tag CU Facebook Init is fired.

Now, let’s add a Facebook “Like”-button to the html of your page:


<div class="fb-like" data-href="http://yourdomain.name" data-layout="standard" data-action="like" data-show-faces="true" data-share="true"></div>

Be sure to fill out the data-href-attribute with the correct url for the test-page (either a real domain or your localtunnel url).
If the url is always the url of the page, it might be useful to write a javascript that updates this to:

window.location.href

Save and refresh the page – click on “Like” a couple of times – and notice the tag UA Social Media being triggered.

See the interactions in UA

Now go to Universal Analytics. Be sure to wait some time in order to have the data saved in UA (at least a couple of minutes!).

Now, go to Acquisition > Social > Plugins
Be sure to choose todays date in the date-range in the upper, right corner.

Now, hopefully (!) you have the entries you just created.
Click on Social Source and Action.

You should see the entries:

Facebook : Like
Facebook : Unlike

— along with a counter!

Happy tracking.
